newsitem.title: UK: Argos slides after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Argos slides after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in catalogue retailer Argos Plc fell on Monday after the company warned that first half profits were unlikely to match those seen last year.
The shares slid to a low of 620p immediately after the news and stood 21-1/2p lower at 626p by 1041 GMT.
"Argos did indicate in March that it would find it difficult to improve over the first half of last year," said Roy Maconochie, stores analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.

"But sales have slowed and are now only up 5-1/2 percent like-for-like after being up 7 percent after ten weeks," he said, adding that the shares looked fairly valued around their current 620-630p price range.

"Profits are affected by a three million downside on net interest receipts following the special dividend payment last year and because they are against the very strong first half last year," Maconochie said. "These are special factors and there's no reason for the market to have knocked Kingfisher 12p as well."
Shares in Kingfisher fell 12p to 700-1/2 in sympathy.
The analyst said he expected to cut his full-year profit forecast for Argos to 150 million stg from 154 million stg previously. In the first half, Maconochie expects to see profits of 28 million stg.
